title: Finding FB2-REV-FND-000037: the four remaining red tests assert an oracle the shipped CMock configuration cannot express for a void* queue buffer, and the only test-side substitute is provably vacuous; the defect is in conf/unit, not in the tests' intent and not in the product's runtime behaviour
lifecycle_status_note: 'draft': this record states a measured root cause for four of the five remaining red tests, established by re-diagnosis from source and by four controlled experiments that were each reverted. No test was changed. No human reviewer has confirmed the analysis and human approval remains 'pending'. This record makes no MISRA conformance claim, no tool-qualification claim and no certification claim of any kind.

revision_history.author: verification_engineer
revision_history.description: First record. Independent re-diagnosis of all five remaining red tests from source, with four controlled experiments (each reverted) and two independent full 313-test sweeps before and after. Corrects the task premise that named tests/unit/app/driver/afe/nxp/mc33775a/config/test_nxp_mc33775a_cfg.c as one of the five: that file passes and is an empty test shell. Records that the void*-queue-buffer case is a fourth, distinct cause not covered by the A/B/C taxonomy of FB2-REV-FND-000033, and that the content-comparison substitute is provably vacuous for this argument.

evidence: SCOPE, as measured. The suite is 313 tests: 208 pass, 5 fail, 100 do not build, 877 assertions tested / 847 passed / 27 failed. Two independent full sweeps from a separately provisioned build root produced identical results on every axis, with zero outcome changes and zero per-test assertion-count changes. The five failing tests are tests/unit/app/driver/afe/debug/can/test_debug_can.c (3 assertions), tests/unit/app/driver/afe/nxp/mc33775a/test_nxp_mc33775a_i2c.c (7), tests/unit/app/driver/can/cbs/rx/test_can_cbs_rx_afe_cell-temperatures.c (1), tests/unit/app/driver/can/cbs/rx/test_can_cbs_rx_afe_cell-voltages.c (1) and tests/unit/app/driver/phy/test_dp83869.c (15 reported). (0) CORRECTION OF THE TASK PREMISE, measured: the fourth test named in the task, tests/unit/app/driver/afe/nxp/mc33775a/config/test_nxp_mc33775a_cfg.c, is NOT failing. Its outcome is 'pass', with Ceedling's summary TESTED: 1 / PASSED: 0 / FAILED: 0 / IGNORED: 1. Reading the file shows why: it is a 78-line shell containing only setUp() at :72 and tearDown() at :75, zero functions matching 'void test', a '@details TODO' stub at :50 and an empty 'Test Cases' section. It therefore registers no test case and executes no assertion. Its green verdict carries no coverage. The genuinely failing fourth test is test_nxp_mc33775a_i2c.c. This correction is material because acting on the premise would have edited a file that is not red. (1) THE DECLARATIONS, read from source: src/app/task/os/os.h:395 declares 'OS_STD_RETURN_e OS_ReceiveFromQueue(OS_QUEUE xQueue, void *const pvBuffer, uint32_t ticksToWait)' and src/app/task/os/os.h:414 declares 'OS_STD_RETURN_e OS_SendToBackOfQueue(OS_QUEUE xQueue, const void *const pvItemToQueue, uint32_t ticksToWait)'. Both payload parameters are untyped. (2) THE COMPARISON CMock ACTUALLY EMITS, read from the CMock 2.7.2 generator source rather than inferred, at lib/cmock_generator_utils.rb:206-210, inside lookup_expect_type: 'elsif arg[:ptr?] && !@arrays && void_pointer_type?(c_type)' followed by the in-source comment 'void* cannot be safely dereferenced; without the array plugin there is no way to specify depth, so fall back to comparing the pointer value itself' and the result "['UNITY_TEST_ASSERT_EQUAL_PTR', '']". conf/unit/app_project_posix.yml:368-369 sets ':memcmp_if_unknown: true' and ':when_ptr: :compare_data', i.e. it REQUESTS a content comparison, and CMock silently downgrades it to pointer identity for a void* parameter. Observed verbatim, e.g. test_can_cbs_rx_afe_cell-temperatures.c:287 'Expected 0x000000016D312050 Was 0x000000016D311FC0:Function OS_SendToBackOfQueue Argument pvItemToQueue'. (3) EXPERIMENT 1 - RETYPING THE EXPECTED ARGUMENT TO THE PRODUCT'S ACTUAL STRUCT TYPE STILL FAILS. Applied to test_can_cbs_rx_afe_cell-voltages.c:293 only, replacing '(void *)&messageData' (a uint64_t) with '(void *)&expectedQueueItem' of type CAN_CAN2AFE_CELL_VOLTAGES_QUEUE_s. Result: the same failure, same mechanism, at the new line 295: 'Expected 0x000000016D002030 Was 0x000000016D001FA8:Function OS_SendToBackOfQueue Argument pvItemToQueue'. The comparison is selected from the PARAMETER type in os.h, not from the type of the test's argument, so retyping cannot help. Reverted; the file is byte-identical to HEAD. (4) WHY IDENTITY IS UNREACHABLE, read from the module under test in each case: the product's buffer is a function-local, so its address is not nameable by the test. src/app/driver/can/cbs/rx/can_cbs_rx_afe_cell-temperatures.c:181 'CAN_CAN2AFE_CELL_TEMPERATURES_QUEUE_s canrx_canCellTemperatures = {0};' is sent at :186. src/app/driver/can/cbs/rx/can_cbs_rx_afe_cell-voltages.c:168 'CAN_CAN2AFE_CELL_VOLTAGES_QUEUE_s canrx_canCellVoltages = {0};' is sent at :173. src/app/driver/afe/debug/can/debug_can.c:236 and :310 declare 'decan_canCellVoltagesFromQueue' and 'decan_canCellTemperaturesFromQueue' as function-locals, received at :239 and :311. src/app/driver/afe/nxp/mc33775a/nxp_mc33775a_i2c.c declares 'AFE_I2C_QUEUE_s transactionData' as a function-local at :259, :290, :330 and :367. The product is correct in every case: src/app/driver/config/can_cfg.h:196-201 documents CAN_CAN2AFE_CELL_TEMPERATURES_QUEUE_s as the 'data unit to be transferred in ftsk_canToAfeCellTemperaturesQueue' and :202-205 the same for ftsk_canToAfeCellVoltagesQueue, so the object the product sends is the declared item type of the queue it sends it to. (5) EXPERIMENT 2 - THE CONTENT ORACLE IS PROVABLY VACUOUS FOR THIS ARGUMENT. A temporary CMock _Stub callback on OS_SendToBackOfQueue was installed in test_can_cbs_rx_afe_cell-voltages.c and the real payload was dumped at the moment of the call, in both RT1/2 and RT2/2. Measured output, twice: '[EXP] payload bytes: 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00  (size=14)'. The payload is 14 bytes (the true size of CAN_CAN2AFE_CELL_VOLTAGES_QUEUE_s) and every byte is zero. The cause is that the RT1/2 and RT2/2 fixtures register CAN_RxGetSignalDataFromMessageData_Expect without the matching _ReturnThruPtr_pCanSignal, and CMock's expect plugin emits argument CHECKS only - lib/cmock_generator_plugin_expect.rb mock_implementation_always_check_args and mock_implementation_might_check_args only call @utils.code_verify_an_arg_expectation and never write an out-parameter. So the packed value is identically zero whatever the packing logic does, and a content comparison can only ever compare zeros with zeros. It cannot detect a wrong mux value, a wrong cell voltage or a wrong invalid flag, i.e. none of the logic under test. The sibling case in the same file is NOT affected and is genuinely non-vacuous: testCANRX_GetCanAfeCellVoltagesFromMessage registers CAN_RxGetSignalDataFromMessageData_ReturnThruPtr_pCanSignal and asserts real extracted values, so the extraction logic is already covered; the RT1/2 and RT2/2 blocks are deliberately only about the call sequence. Reverted; the file is byte-identical to HEAD. (6) THE CMock CALLBACK ROUTES, quoted from the generator, so that no later reader has to re-derive them. lib/cmock_generator_plugin_callback.rb:57-69 mock_implementation_precheck emits 'if (!Mock.X_CallbackBool && Mock.X_CallbackFunctionPointer != NULL) { ...cb(...); return; }' - a full escape from the mock, so _Stub (which sets CallbackBool=0 at :87) discards the CalledMore, the strict-ordering and the argument assertions and the ReturnVal. _AddCallback sets CallbackBool=1 at :78 and the callback is emitted by mock_implementation at :47-55, which lib/cmock_generator.rb:361 places AFTER the CalledMore assertion at :353 and after the order checks at :356-358 - so _AddCallback preserves the check chain but therefore also preserves the failing argument check and cannot make the test pass. Both _Stub (:88) and _AddCallback (:79) set CallbackCalls = 0 on every registration, so re-registering a stub between two phases of a test erases the first phase's count. With ':callback_include_count: true' (conf/unit/app_project_posix.yml:371) the callback signature takes a fourth 'int cmock_num_calls' parameter, which the experiment confirmed at compile time. A trap specific to this project: lib/cmock_generator_plugin_callback.rb:31-37 derives '#define X_StubWithCallback X_#{callback_after_arg_check ? AddCallback : Stub}' and the shipped conf sets ':callback_after_arg_check: false' (conf/unit/app_project_posix.yml:372), so in this project X_StubWithCallback expands to the full-bypass _Stub, not to the checking _AddCallback. (7) BLAST RADIUS, measured rather than extrapolated. 74 OS_*Queue_Expect* call sites exist across 10 test files. Five of those files are red today and are the four tests of this finding plus test_nxp_mc33775a_i2c.c. Four of the remaining five do not build, so their identical expectation is unobserved: tests/unit/app/application/ethernet/test_ethernet.c:148 passes '&testReceivedSocket' where src/app/application/ethernet/ethernet.c:138-139 has a function-local 'Socket_t connectedSocket' and passes '&connectedSocket'; tests/unit/app/driver/can/test_can.c:394,409,424 pass '&message' and :404 passes '&dummyMessageBuffer' where src/app/driver/can/can.c:996-1000 has a function-local 'message'; tests/unit/app/driver/afe/adi/ades1830/test_adi_ades1830.c:201,206 pass '(void *)&testRequest' where src/app/driver/afe/adi/common/ades183x/adi_ades183x.c:373 passes '&request', the address of the by-value parameter of ADI_MakeRequest(AFE_REQUEST_e request) at :369, which is a distinct stack object in the callee frame; tests/unit/app/driver/can/cbs/rx/test_can_cbs_rx_f_debug.c:313,683 pass '(void *)&timeData' where src/app/driver/can/cbs/rx/can_cbs_rx_f_debug.c:590 has a function-local 'RTC_TIME_DATA_s timeData = {0}'. The tenth file, tests/unit/app/driver/imd/bender/iso165c/test_bender_iso165c.c, is NOT claimed to be affected: src/app/driver/imd/bender/iso165c/bender_iso165c.c:441,475 pass the propagated parameter '(void *)pCanMessage', so identity can hold there, and the corresponding test tests/unit/app/driver/can/cbs/rx/test_can_cbs_rx_imd_bender-iso165c-info.c passes 15/15 in the same sweep. (8) SEPARATELY CONFIRMED, NOT CHANGED: test_dp83869.c was re-diagnosed and its fault re-reproduced independently in this work. See FB2-REV-FND-000035, which already records it; the independent confirmation and the corrected per-case tally are appended to FB2-VER-EXE-000015. (9) One build-failure CLASS is nondeterministic and was not treated as a change: tests/unit/app/driver/rtc/test_rtc.c alternates between 'build:strict_diagnostic' and 'build:other' across sweeps (22/23 and 23/22 on the same two runs). The outcome is 'build_failure' either way, the total is 100 either way, and the 313-test outcome set is otherwise bit-identical.
impact: What this costs is verification coverage, not product integrity, and the cost is larger than the 13 red assertions suggest. For four tests the queue payload has no working oracle, so the code path that packs a CAN message and hands it to the AFE task is unverified, and at least four further tests carry the identical expectation behind build failures and will surface the same failure whenever their build problems are fixed. The blast radius is bounded and known: 74 call sites in 10 files, of which 5 files are red, at least 4 more are latent, and 1 is demonstrably not affected. Three remedies were each constructed and each rejected on measurement, not judgement. Retyping the expected argument to the product's struct type: still fails, measured. A _Stub content callback: goes green but the payload compared is 14 zero bytes in both phases, so it constrains nothing that the packing logic controls, and it additionally discards the called-more, strict-ordering and return-value assertions for those calls, as quoted from the CMock generator above. _AddCallback: preserves every check, and therefore preserves the failing one. None of these is a test fix. It would be wrong to present a green run of these four tests as an improvement in verification, because the green would be produced by an assertion that cannot fail for any product defect in the logic under test. This is explicitly not evidence of MISRA conformance, of tool qualification, or of any certification, and no such claim may be inferred from this record.
root_cause: A shipped-configuration defect in conf/unit/app_project_posix.yml, combined with a C language scoping fact, makes the assertion inexpressible rather than merely unmet. conf/unit/app_project_posix.yml:369 asks CMock to ':when_ptr: :compare_data' and :368 sets ':memcmp_if_unknown: true', which is a request for a CONTENT comparison of pointer arguments. CMock cannot honour that request for a void* parameter: it has no way to learn the pointee size, its own generator says so in as many words at lib/cmock_generator_utils.rb:207-209, and it silently falls back to UNITY_TEST_ASSERT_EQUAL_PTR. The downgrade is invisible in the test source, so a test that reads as a content assertion is in fact an identity assertion. The second half is scoping: the code under test correctly declares the queue payload as a function-local and passes its address, and a function-local's address is not expressible in the caller, so identity can never hold no matter what the test passes. The two together produce an assertion that is unsatisfiable by construction on any compiler and any platform, and which the CMock feature set offers no way to replace from the test side without deleting the check or making it vacuous. This is a fourth cause, distinct from the three in FB2-REV-FND-000033: that taxonomy classifies cases where a real content oracle exists and differs in achievability (B) or is not achievable but a partial one is meaningful (C). Here the correct content oracle does not merely differ, it is CONSTANT - the value is provably all-zero because the test's own fixture never supplies an input to the mocked signal extractor - so no field of it carries information. Note what is NOT the cause, so that the distinction is not lost: the void* declarations are not defective, and this record does not re-open FB2-REV-FND-000031's measured conclusion that they are required by the design; and the module under test is not defective, since in every one of the five sites it sends exactly the type can_cfg.h documents for that queue.
resolution: NOT RESOLVED, and deliberately not worked around. No test was changed; the whole of tests/ is byte-identical to HEAD, verified with git status and git diff, and git diff -- src conf tools cli is empty. The correct fix is a decision for the product owner and lives outside tests/: either type or constrain the queue-payload parameter so CMock learns a size, or add ':treat_as:' entries for the specific queue payload types, or load the array plugin and specify a depth. All three are changes to conf/ or to the product API and none was made. What was done instead: the diagnosis was re-derived from source and from the CMock generator rather than inherited; the two candidate test-side remedies were each built, measured and reverted, which is what established that the content oracle is vacuous and that the _Stub route costs checks; the blast radius was measured instead of assumed; and the false element of the task premise was found and is recorded above, so that the empty test_nxp_mc33775a_cfg.c is not mistaken for a fixed test. Two further items are handed on rather than closed: test_nxp_mc33775a_cfg.c contains no test case at all and needs a product-owner decision on whether nxp_mc33775a_cfg.c is meant to be covered; and the four latent files in the blast radius should be expected to fail the same way once their build failures are fixed. Still open and out of scope here, unchanged by this work: the CMock compare_data-on-a-by-value-uint64_t configuration gap at src/app/driver/can/cbs/can_helper.h:131, fixed only in the SIL harness copy of the project file and not in conf/; the test_dp83869.c host-harness limitation in FB2-REV-FND-000035; and the 100 build failures, which another workstream owns.
